extracted.intended_audience: Researchers submitting papers to NeurIPS (machine learning authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist and guidelines authors must complete and include with NeurIPS submissions to ensure reproducibility, transparency, ethics, and responsible reporting. Covers placement, required answers, and detailed criteria (claims, proofs, experiments, data/code, ethics, impacts, human subjects, LLM usage, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist inclusion and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NeurIPS paper checklist must be included in the single-submission PDF file in the specified order: (1) submitted paper; (2) optional technical appendices; (3) the NeurIPS paper checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist is included in the LaTeX style file and must not be removed. The checklist does NOT count towards the page limit. Papers not including the checklist will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer format and justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For each checklist question, authors should answer yes, no, or n/a (Not Applicable or Not Available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may optionally write a short (1–2 sentence) justification for answers; if answering 'yes', point to section(s) in the paper or supplement that support the answer. Answers are visible to reviewers, area chairs, senior area chairs, and ethics reviewers. 'Yes' is generally preferable but 'no' or 'n/a' is acceptable with justification; such answers are not by themselves grounds for rejection. Use best judgement and elaborate where answers are nuanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the main claims in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper's contributions and scope? Claims should match theoretical and experimental results in terms of expected generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions should be clearly stated along with important assumptions and limitations. Aspirational goals are acceptable if it is clear they are not achieved. Enter yes/no/n/a and provide explanation or pointer to supporting sections if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a separate 'Limitations' section discussing strong assumptions, robustness to assumption violations, and scope of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how assumptions might be violated in practice and implications, scope of experiments (e.g., few datasets or runs), and factors influencing performance (e.g., resolution, lighting). Reviewers are instructed not to penalize honesty about limitations; answer 'NA' if the paper has no limitations, 'No' if limitations exist but are not discussed in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory, assumptions, and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: If including theoretical results, state the full set of assumptions for all results and include complete proofs of all theoretical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in theorem statements. Proofs may be in the main paper or supplement, but authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch in the main text for intuition. Informal proofs in the core must be complemented by formal proofs in appendix/supplement. Theorems/lemmas used in proofs should be properly referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental result reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For datasets or models, provide steps taken to make results reproducible or verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility can include: releasing code and data, detailed replication instructions, providing hosted model access, releasing checkpoints, or other appropriate means. If closed-source, provide a reasonable access path. Authors should choose reproducibility measures appropriate to the contribution and explain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access to data and code
rubrics_metrics.description: If experiments were run, did the authors include code, data, and instructions needed to reproduce the main experimental results (in supplemental material or as a URL)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions should contain exact commands and environment needed. While release is encouraged, 'no' is acceptable (e.g., proprietary code). Papers cannot be rejected simply for lacking code unless it is central to the contribution (e.g., new open-source benchmark). At submission time, release anonymized versions to preserve anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental setting and details
rubrics_metrics.description: If experiments were run, specify all training details (data splits, hyperparameters, how hyperparameters were chosen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important details should appear in the main paper; full details can be in code, appendix, or supplement. The experimental setting should be presented sufficiently to appreciate results and make sense of them. Answer 'NA' if no experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment statistical significance and error bars
rubrics_metrics.description: Report error bars, confidence intervals, or other information about statistical significance for experiments supporting main claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which factors variability/error bars capture (e.g., train/test split, initialization), explain the method for calculating error bars (formula, library, bootstrap), and state assumptions (e.g., normality). Clarify whether error bars show standard deviation or standard error. For asymmetric distributions, avoid symmetric error bars that yield impossible values. If error bars appear in tables/plots, explain their calculation and reference the corresponding figures/tables. 'NA' means no experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments compute resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient information on compute resources (type of workers, memory, run time) needed to reproduce experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate compute type (CPU/GPU), internal cluster vs cloud, memory and storage, compute per experimental run and estimated total compute, and disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported (e.g., preliminary/failed experiments). 'NA' if no experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS Code of Ethics compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you read the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and ensured that your research conforms to it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If special circumstances require deviation from the Code of Ethics, explain them while preserving anonymity (e.g., due to jurisdictional laws). Answers are visible to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impacts / potential negative societal impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: If appropriate, discuss potential negative societal impacts of the work (malicious/unintended uses, fairness, privacy, security).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider harms when the technology is used as intended, when it gives incorrect results, and from misuse. Provide possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release, defenses, monitoring mechanisms). Foundational research with no direct applications may legitimately have limited discussion, but if a direct path to negative applications exists it should be pointed out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards for high-risk models and datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: If models or datasets have high risk for misuse (e.g., pretrained LLMs, scraped datasets), describe safeguards for responsible release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards may include usage restrictions, gated access, usage guidelines, and measures to avoid releasing unsafe images. Authors are encouraged to make a best faith effort; many papers will not require such safeguards but should consider them when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses for used assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If using existing assets (code, data, models), cite creators and respect license and terms of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite original paper, state version and provide URL if possible, name the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0). If data was scraped, state the copyright and terms of service of the source. If releasing assets, include license, copyright, and terms of use. When repackaging datasets, state both original and derived licenses. If license information is not found, contact the asset creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for released assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If releasing new assets (datasets, code, models), document them and provide details alongside the assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured templates to communicate training details, license, limitations, consent procedures, etc. Discuss how consent was obtained from people whose assets are used. At submission time, anonymize assets (e.g., anonymized URL or zip). 'NA' if no new assets are released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: If using crowdsourcing or human subjects, include full text of participant instructions and screenshots, and details about compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information can be in supplemental material, but if the main contribution involves human subjects include details in the main paper. Per the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers must be paid at least the minimum wage in their country. 'NA' if not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB approvals and participant risk description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any potential participant risks and obtain Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals or equivalent, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IRB approval was obtained, clearly state this in the paper. For initial submissions, do not include information that would break anonymity (e.g., the institution conducting the review). Recognize that IRB procedures vary by country/institution and follow NeurIPS Code of Ethics and institutional guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of LLM usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe usage of large language models (LLMs) if they are an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If LLMs are used only for writing, editing, or formatting and do not impact core methodology or originality, declaration is not required. Answer 'NA' if core method development does not involve LLMs. Refer to the Main Track Handbook for details on what should be described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving anonymity in releases and IRB statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve author and institutional anonymity when releasing code, data, assets, or IRB information for initial submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create anonymized URLs or anonymized zip files for assets. Do not include institution-identifying details (e.g., the IRB institution) in initial submissions. Where explanation of special circumstances is required, ensure anonymity is maintained.
